title: QASiNa: Religious Domain Question Answering using Sirah Nabawiyah
findings: The extractive model XLM-R performed best on the QASiNa dataset. In contrast, both ChatGPT-3.5 and GPT-4 performed poorly on extractive metrics like Exact Match (EM) and F1-Score but achieved high Substring Match scores. This indicates that even when instructed to be extractive, these generative models tend to provide excessive interpretations, making them unsuitable for question answering in the Islamic religious domain where unauthorized interpretation is prohibited.

measurement_description: The benchmark measures the ability of language models to perform extractive question answering on Islamic historical texts (Sirah Nabawiyah) in Indonesian. It specifically evaluates whether models can provide answers directly from the given context without generating their own interpretations (tafseer), which is a restricted practice in Islam.
